title: Small employer health insurance premiums credit
summary: Review employer-paid employee health premiums for a potential small-employer credit; coverage expense alone does not establish eligibility.
scope_note: Employer business; partnership or S corporation credits can pass through to owners. Owner personal coverage is not automatically qualifying employee coverage. This initial screening scope covers taxable businesses; tax-exempt routes require separate review.
claimant_note: The employer business is the screening subject; pass-through reporting and owner allocations require review.

conditions.description: Employer offers health benefits; offering benefits alone does not establish a claim.
2025 eligible-employer workforce and average-wage tests, including aggregation and excluded workers, must be established.
Qualifying premium-payment arrangement and SHOP coverage or an applicable exception must be documented.
Credit-period history must permit a 2025 claim; the allowed credit reduces the related premium deduction.

missing_evidence: Annual payroll hours, wages, ownership and related-business census
SHOP policy or exception records and employer-paid premium evidence
Prior credit claims and deduction adjustments

title: Small employer retirement plan startup costs credit
summary: Review qualifying costs to establish or administer an eligible retirement plan, including employee retirement education.
scope_note: Eligible employer business; pass-through credits may reach owners through entity allocations. Personal IRA contributions are outside this startup-cost rule.
claimant_note: The employer business is the screening subject; pass-through reporting and owner allocations require review.

sources.title: Instructions for Form 8881 (12/2025), Part I Section 1

conditions.description: Prior-year employee and compensation tests, predecessor and controlled-group rules must be checked.
Prior plans covering substantially the same employees can prevent eligibility; the eligible plan must include a non-highly compensated eligible employee.
2025 must fall within the permitted startup credit years; credited startup costs reduce the related deduction.

missing_evidence: Prior-year payroll and employee eligibility census
Plan adoption, effective date, prior-plan and related-employer history
Startup or administration invoices, education costs and prior Form 8881 claims

title: Disabled access credit
summary: Review eligible small-business expenditures to provide disability access and comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act.
scope_note: Eligible small business making access expenditures; pass-through credit recipients use their allocated credit. An owner's disability alone does not establish a business claim.
claimant_note: The employer business is the screening subject; pass-through reporting and owner allocations require review.

sources.title: Form 8826 (Rev. September 2017), current IRS revision, instructions on page 2
sources.notes: Supporting current IRS revision, not a 2025 edition.

conditions.description: Prior-year business-size and aggregation tests must be checked.
Costs must be reasonable, necessary eligible access expenditures; applicable facility-date exclusions and standards require review.
The credited portion cannot also be deducted, capitalized or used for another credit; coordinate any section 190 deduction.

missing_evidence: Prior-year receipts, workforce and related-business records
Access-work scope, facility placed-in-service history and compliance evidence
Vendor invoices and allocation among credit, deduction and capitalized costs

title: Architectural and transportation barrier removal deduction
summary: Review qualified business costs to remove mobility barriers for people with disabilities or older people that would otherwise be capitalized.
scope_note: Business of any size paying qualifying business costs; the business's tax classification determines reporting. Personal home improvements are not established as business costs by this rule.
claimant_note: The employer business is the screening subject; pass-through reporting and owner allocations require review.

sources.title: Tax benefits for businesses who have employees with disabilities, Barrier Removal Tax Deduction
sources.notes: This IRS guidance is evergreen, not a 2025 edition. The library applies it to a 2025 review; no deduction amount has been calculated.

conditions.description: Work must qualify as architectural or transportation barrier removal; ordinary renovation is not sufficient evidence.
Applicable annual limits and separate-expense reporting require review.
Section 44 and section 190 may apply in the same year when both requirements are met; exclude the credited portion from the deduction.

missing_evidence: Business property and barrier-removal work records
Detailed invoices and evidence of otherwise-capitalized costs
Tax-year expenditure totals and section 44 cost allocation

title: Work opportunity tax credit
summary: Review qualifying 2025 hires for an employer credit after required state workforce certification; payroll alone is insufficient.
scope_note: Hiring employer business, including taxable employers of any size; not a personal credit for the hired worker. Tax-exempt employer rules are narrower. This initial screening scope covers taxable businesses; tax-exempt routes require separate review.
claimant_note: The employer business is the screening subject; pass-through reporting and owner allocations require review.

sources.title: Work Opportunity Tax Credit
sources.notes: Evergreen IRS guidance checked for the 2025 hiring period; 2025 is the review year, not the publication date.

sources.title: Instructions for Form 5884, current IRS instructions, deduction reduction
sources.notes: Supporting current IRS revision, not a 2025 edition.

conditions.description: Worker must belong to a qualifying targeted group and begin work on or before December 31, 2025.
Form 8850 pre-screening must be completed by the job-offer date and timely submitted to the state workforce agency; certification is required.
Qualifying wages, work hours and rehire exclusions require review; coordinate other credits using the same wages and the wage deduction adjustment.

missing_evidence: Dated offer, start date and Form 8850 submission evidence
State workforce agency certification
Payroll hours, qualifying wages, rehire history and other wage-based credit allocations

title: IRC 179 — Election to expense qualifying business property
summary: A business may elect to expense qualifying property placed in service in 2025, subject to dollar, investment and business-income limits.
scope_note: Sole proprietors, partnerships, S corporations and other corporations; estates and trusts cannot elect.
claimant_note: Business taxpayer; partnership or S corporation elects and allocates to owners, who separately apply their limits.

conditions.description: Identify purchased qualifying property used predominantly (more than 50%) in an actively conducted trade or business and placed in service in 2025.
Apply the 2025 dollar, investment and business-income limits; partnership/S-corporation and owner limits both matter.
Document the election and owner allocations; review basis, carryovers and possible recapture.
Coordinate asset basis with bonus and regular depreciation; do not deduct the same basis twice.

missing_evidence: Asset invoices, seller relationship and ownership
Placed-in-service dates and business-use records
Entity tax classification, income, K-1 allocations, basis and prior depreciation/elections

title: IRC 168(k) — Special depreciation allowance
summary: First-year bonus depreciation may apply to qualifying business property. The 2025 law restored a 100% allowance for certain property acquired and placed in service after January 19, 2025.
scope_note: Business taxpayers owning qualifying depreciable property, including sole proprietors, partnerships and corporations.
claimant_note: Tax owner of depreciable property; entity-owned assets are handled in the entity depreciation computation.

conditions.description: Confirm property class, acquisition rules and placed-in-service date; new and certain used property may qualify.
Do not apply the restored allowance to all 2025 purchases: property acquired before January 20, 2025 requires separate phase-down review.
Review exclusions, business use, and any election out or transitional election.
Compute after section 179 and other basis reductions, before regular depreciation; do not reuse deducted basis.

missing_evidence: Asset owner, invoices and acquisition agreements
Property class, original/used status and business-use percentage
Placed-in-service records, basis adjustments and depreciation elections

title: IRC 45B — Employer FICA tax credit on certain employee tips
summary: An employer may claim a general business credit for qualifying employer Social Security and Medicare taxes on employee tips. For tax years beginning after 2024, specified beauty services are included.
scope_note: Food/beverage employers and employers providing specified barbering/beauty services, subject to the tip and payroll conditions.
claimant_note: Employer; partnerships and S corporations report the credit for pass-through to partners/shareholders.

sources.title: 2025 Form 8846, Credit for Employer Social Security and Medicare Taxes Paid on Certain Employee Tips (including instructions)

conditions.description: Employees receive customer tips for providing, delivering or serving food/beverages for consumption, with customary tipping; or for customary-tipped barbering/hair care, nail care, esthetics, or body/spa treatments.
Employer paid or incurred employer Social Security and Medicare taxes on those tips during the tax year; distinguish tips from service charges.
Apply the industry-specific minimum-wage adjustment and wage-base computation, plus general business credit limits.
Reduce the employer payroll-tax deduction by the credit amount.

missing_evidence: Employee tip reports, payroll tax records and service/industry description
Monthly employee hours and non-tip wages
General business credit position and any K-1 allocation

title: IRC 199A — Qualified business income deduction
summary: An owner-level deduction based on qualified business income may apply for 2025, subject to taxable-income and other limitations.
scope_note: Owners of sole proprietorships and pass-through businesses; C-corporation income is excluded.
claimant_note: Individual owner, or eligible estate/trust; not the partnership or S corporation itself.

conditions.description: Establish a qualifying trade or business and compute net QBI, including attributable deductions and applicable loss carryovers.
Exclude employee wages, S-corporation reasonable compensation and partner guaranteed payments from QBI.
Review taxable income, filing status, specified-service rules and applicable wage/property limitations.
Use owner-level Form 8995 or 8995-A; partnerships/S corporations provide supporting K-1 information.

missing_evidence: Owner filing status, taxable income and capital-gain information
Schedule C or K-1 QBI statements and business classification
W-2 wages, qualified-property information and loss/deduction carryovers

title: IRC 162(l) — Self-employed health insurance deduction
summary: A qualifying self-employed individual may deduct qualifying health insurance premiums on the individual return, subject to business-income and coverage restrictions.
scope_note: Sole proprietors, qualifying partners and qualifying more-than-2% S-corporation shareholders; this is an individual deduction.
claimant_note: Individual self-employed owner or qualifying more-than-2% S-corporation shareholder.

conditions.description: Insurance must be established under the business and satisfy the net-profit/net-earnings or S-corporation wage requirements.
For a policy in a partner’s name that the partner pays personally, the partnership must reimburse the premiums and report them as guaranteed payments on Schedule K-1.

For a more-than-2% S-corporation shareholder, corporation-paid/reimbursed premiums must be reported as wages; personally paid shareholder-name policies require corporate reimbursement and W-2 box 1 reporting.
Exclude months when eligible for a subsidized employer plan, including applicable family-employer coverage.
Apply the business-specific earnings limit and coordinate any Marketplace premium tax credit.

missing_evidence: Owner status, business earnings or S-corporation wages
Policy, premium payments and corporate reimbursement records
Form W-2, monthly other-plan eligibility and Marketplace coverage information
For partners: partnership reimbursement and Schedule K-1 guaranteed-payment reporting
